drivingQuestion: Why is a kosher bird resting on the eggs of a non-kosher bird exempt from shiluah haken, given that it is itself a צפור?
outcomeNote: The difficulty against the mishna's second clause is left standing at the end of the packet; no answer appears in the segments given.

segments.he: עוֹף טָמֵא רוֹבֵץ עַל בֵּיצֵי עוֹף טָהוֹר. בִּשְׁלָמָא עוֹף טָמֵא רוֹבֵץ עַל בֵּיצֵי טָהוֹר – בָּעֵינַן ״צִפּוֹר״ וְלֵיכָּא, אֶלָּא עוֹף טָהוֹר רוֹבֵץ עַל בֵּיצֵי עוֹף טָמֵא – הָא ״צִפּוֹר״ הוּא!
segments.en: § The mishna states: If «a non-kosher bird is resting upon the eggs of a kosher bird,» or a kosher bird is resting upon the eggs of a non-kosher bird, one is exempt from sending away the bird. The Gemara objects: «Granted,» it is understandable that one is exempt in a case where «a non-kosher bird is resting upon the eggs of a kosher» bird, since «we require» a kosher bird, as the verse uses the word «“tzippor”» (Deuteronomy 22:6) in this context, which the Gemara earlier (139b) interpreted as a reference to a kosher bird, «and» this bird «is not» kosher. «But» in a case where «a kosher bird is resting upon the eggs of a non-kosher bird, it is a tzippor,» a kosher bird, and one should be required to send it away.

moves.cueHe: אלא עוף טהור רובץ על ביצי עוף טמא
moves.summary: presses the second case: that bird is a צפור, so why is one exempt from sending it away?
moves.about: why the mishna also exempts a kosher bird resting on the eggs of a non-kosher bird, when that bird is itself a צפור
